issues.detail: Authentication is left as '// ... same auth setup as other Graph API skills' and the empty 'Common Patterns' heading is a dangling stub, and the Guidelines say images can be 'base64 in multipart request' while no multipart example is shown.

There are no error-handling instructions for 429 throttling, 401/403 token or consent failures, or 404 on missing notebooks, sections or pages. Nothing covers pagination via @odata.nextLink, failed PATCH targets, or the fact that Microsoft Search is a poor fit for finding OneNote pages (filetype:one matches files, not pages).

The auth snippet is not runnable because token acquisition is omitted, `userId` and `graphClient` are never defined, and the examples are prose narratives of REST calls, not code or command sequences. The second Search snippet queries driveItem with 'filetype:one', which would not return individual pages.

The two examples describe agent behavior in prose rather than showing the concrete request and response, and the example 2 search uses `$filter=contains(title, ...)` without a note that this filter is limited on the pages collection.

scenarios.name: append-update-to-existing-page
scenarios.rationale: Response A matches the rubric: it finds the page with a contains(title, ...) filter, takes its id, and PATCHes /content with target 'body', action 'append', position 'after' and a paragraph with data-tag="important" containing 1,250 and 900, while Response B does no API calls, gives manual instructions, and wrongly says Graph can't set the Important tag.

scenarios.name: background-service-auth-pitfall
scenarios.rationale: Both say app-only auth was retired on March 31, 2025 and that delegated permissions with a signed-in user are required, and both show GET .../pages/{id}/content returning HTML; A names Notes.ReadWrite.All with admin consent as the rubric asks and gives a clean working example, while B recommends Notes.Read.All instead, never names Notes.ReadWrite.All as the required scope, and includes a broken placeholder code block that it then has to correct.
